chunks: ʿAlī, from his father, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ghālib, from his father, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, who said:

I asked ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام about a man who struck a pregnant woman with his foot, and she cast out what was in her womb dead. He said: “If it was a drop of fluid, then twenty dinars are due from him.” I said: What is the limit of the drop of fluid? He said: “It is that which has fallen into the womb and remained settled there for forty days.”

He said: “If she cast it out while it was a clot, then forty dinars are due from him.” I said: What is the limit of the clot? He said: “It is that which, when it falls into the womb, remains settled there for eighty days.”

He said: “If she cast it out while it was a morsel of flesh, then sixty dinars are due from him.” I said: What is the limit of the morsel of flesh? He said: “It is that which, when it falls into the womb, remains settled there for one hundred and twenty days.”

He said: “If she cast it out while it was a formed living being, having bone and flesh, with its limbs arranged, and the spirit of intellect had been breathed into it, then a full indemnity is due from him.”

I said to him: Inform me about its transformation in her womb from one state to another—was that with a spirit, or without a spirit? He said: “With the spirit of the nourishment of life, ancient and transmitted through the loins of men and the wombs of women. Were it not that the spirit of the nourishment of life was in it, it would not have transformed from one state after another in the womb, and then there would not be indemnity upon the one who killed it while it was in that state.”

key_terms.الرَّحِمِ: the womb, where the fetus develops through successive stages
key_terms.دِينَارًا: a gold monetary unit used here to quantify indemnity
key_terms.دِيَةً كَامِلَةً: full blood-money due for the killing of a fully formed fetus
key_terms.رُوحُ الْعَقْلِ: the spirit of intellect breathed into the fully formed fetus
key_terms.عَلَقَةٌ: the embryonic stage described as a clot
key_terms.مُضْغَةٌ: the embryonic stage described as a morsel of flesh
key_terms.نُطْفَةً: the earliest embryonic stage described as a drop of fluid in the womb

ai.seo_question: What diyah is due for killing a fetus at different stages of development according to Imam ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith sets graded diyah amounts for causing the death of a fetus according to its stage of development in the womb, from nuṭfah to a fully formed being. It also distinguishes between developmental life in the womb and the later breathing of the spirit of intellect, while affirming legal liability for destroying the fetus even in earlier stages.
